Contact us today to learn more about how we can help streamline your content management and unlock the full potential of your business information. After all, we've been in the business of making technology work for you since 1914, and we're just getting started.

title: Guarding the Gates: The Importance of Intrusion Detection for Your Business
htmlTitle: Intrusion Detection: Guarding the Gates for Business
author: Van Ausdall & Farrar
teaser: From sophisticated hackers to opportunistic malware, the risks to your company's valuable data and systems are numerous. Talk to our specialists for guidance.
metaDescription: From sophisticated hackers to opportunistic malware, the risks to your company's valuable data and systems are numerous. Talk to our specialists for guidance.
bodyHtml:
Businesses face an ever-growing array of cybersecurity threats. From sophisticated hackers to opportunistic malware, the risks to your company's valuable data and systems are numerous. That's why it's crucial to have robust defenses in place, and one of the most important tools in your cybersecurity arsenal is intrusion detection. At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we've been helping businesses stay secure since 1914, and we're here to shed some light on this critical aspect of IT security.

What is Intrusion Detection?

Intrusion detection is like having a vigilant security guard for your network. It's a system designed to monitor your network traffic and system activities for any suspicious behavior or policy violations. When it detects something amiss, it alerts your IT team so they can investigate and respond promptly.

Think of it as the high-tech equivalent of those motion-activated lights you might have outside your home. Just as those lights deter potential burglars and alert you to unexpected activity, intrusion detection systems (IDS) keep a watchful eye on your digital domain.

Types of Intrusion Detection Systems

There are two main types of intrusion detection systems:

  1. Network-based IDS (NIDS): These systems monitor network traffic for suspicious activity. They're like the security cameras of your digital infrastructure, keeping an eye on everything that comes in and out.
  2. Host-based IDS (HIDS): These focus on individual devices or endpoints. Think of them as the security guards stationed at each entrance of a building, checking IDs and looking out for anything unusual.

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we understand that every business is unique, and we work with you to determine the best mix of intrusion detection systems for your specific needs.

Why is Intrusion Detection Important?

You might be wondering, "Why do I need intrusion detection? Isn't a good firewall enough?" Well, while firewalls are certainly important (think of them as the locks on your doors), intrusion detection adds an extra layer of security. Here's why it's crucial:

  • Early Warning System: Intrusion detection can alert you to potential threats before they cause significant damage. It's like having a smoke detector for your network, it gives you a chance to respond before a small problem becomes a full-blown disaster.
  • Compliance: Many industry regulations require some form of intrusion detection. If you're in healthcare, finance, or government contracting, having a robust IDS isn't just smart. It's often mandatory.
  • Insider Threat Detection: Not all threats come from outside. IDS can help detect unusual activity from within your organization, helping to mitigate risks from disgruntled employees or compromised accounts.
  • Forensic Analysis: In the event of a security incident, intrusion detection systems provide valuable data for post-incident analysis. It's like having a security camera that not only alerts you to break-ins but also helps you figure out how they happened.

Intrusion Detection and Van Ausdall & Farrar's Services

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we've been helping businesses leverage technology to improve their operations since the days of Thomas Edison. While the technology has certainly changed since 1914, our commitment to providing value-driven solutions hasn't. Here's how our services integrate with and support robust intrusion detection:

1. Managed IT Solutions

Our Managed IT Solutions include comprehensive security measures, with intrusion detection as a key component. We monitor your systems 24/7, ensuring that any suspicious activity is caught and addressed promptly. It's like having a team of expert security guards watching over your digital assets round the clock.

2. Cloud Solutions

As businesses increasingly move to the cloud, the need for robust security measures, including intrusion detection, becomes even more critical. Our Cloud Solutions incorporate state-of-the-art security measures to protect your data and applications, whether they're hosted on-premises, in the cloud, or in a hybrid environment.

3. Network Solutions

Our Network Solutions team can help design and implement a network architecture that incorporates intrusion detection at key points. We ensure that your network isn't just fast and reliable, but also secure and monitored.

4. IT Support

Our IT Support team is well-versed in managing and responding to alerts from intrusion detection systems. They're like the rapid response team, ready to spring into action at the first sign of trouble.

Implementing Intrusion Detection: Best Practices

Implementing an effective intrusion detection system isn't just about installing some software and forgetting about it. Here are some best practices to consider:

  1. Regular Updates: Cyber threats are constantly evolving, and your IDS needs to keep up. Regular updates ensure your system can detect the latest threats.
  2. Tuning: Every network is unique, and your IDS needs to be tuned to your specific environment to reduce false positives and ensure it's focusing on the most relevant threats.
  3. Integration: Your IDS should be part of a larger security ecosystem, working in concert with firewalls, antivirus software, and other security measures.
  4. Response Plan: Having an IDS is great, but you also need a plan for how to respond when it detects something. This is where Van Ausdall & Farrar's expertise comes in handy, we can help you develop and implement effective response strategies.
  5. Staff Training: Your employees are often your first line of defense. Training them to recognize and report suspicious activity can complement your technical measures.

The Future of Intrusion Detection

As we look to the future, intrusion detection is evolving to meet new challenges. Here are some trends we're keeping an eye on:

  • AI and Machine Learning: These technologies are making intrusion detection systems smarter and more adaptive, able to detect complex, previously unknown threats.
  • IoT Security: As more devices connect to networks, intrusion detection systems are adapting to monitor and protect these new potential entry points.
  • Cloud-Native Solutions: With the continued shift to cloud computing, we're seeing more cloud-native intrusion detection solutions that are designed to protect distributed, dynamic environments.

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we're committed to staying at the forefront of these developments, ensuring our clients have access to the most effective, up-to-date security solutions.

Conclusion: Partnering for Security

In an age where digital threats are constantly evolving, intrusion detection is a critical component of any comprehensive cybersecurity strategy. It's not just about having the right technology. It's about having the right partner to help you implement, manage, and respond to the insights these systems provide.

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we've been helping businesses navigate technological changes for over a century. From our early days with Thomas Edison's technology to today's advanced cybersecurity solutions, our mission has remained the same: to provide value-driven technology solutions while delivering a world-class customer experience.

We believe that by implementing the right technology, we can improve the human experience, and that includes creating a safer, more secure digital environment for your business to thrive. Whether you're looking to implement a new intrusion detection system, upgrade your existing security measures, or simply want to understand your options better, we're here to help.

Remember, in the world of cybersecurity, you're only as strong as your weakest link. With Van Ausdall & Farrar as your technology partner, you can rest assured that your defenses are robust, up-to-date, and tailored to your specific needs. Let's work together to keep your business safe in the digital age.

Contact us today to learn more about how we can help protect your business with state-of-the-art intrusion detection and comprehensive IT solutions. After all, your security is our business, and we've been perfecting that business since 1914.

title: Dialing into the Future: How VoIP is Transforming Business Communication
htmlTitle: VoIP Is Transforming the Way Businesses Communicate
author: Van Ausdall & Farrar
teaser: As technology continues to evolve, so do the ways we connect with colleagues, clients, and partners. Talk to our specialists about the right solution for you.
metaDescription: As technology continues to evolve, so do the ways we connect with colleagues, clients, and partners. Talk to our specialists about the right solution for you.
bodyHtml:
As technology continues to evolve, so do the ways we connect with colleagues, clients, and partners. One such innovation that has transformed the landscape of business communication is Voice over Internet Protocol, or VoIP. At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we've been at the forefront of communication technology since 1914, and we're excited to share how VoIP is changing the game for businesses of all sizes.

What is VoIP?

VoIP is a technology that allows voice calls to be made over the internet rather than traditional phone lines. Instead of using analog signals, VoIP converts your voice into digital data packets that are transmitted over the internet. This simple yet powerful concept has opened up a world of possibilities for businesses looking to streamline their communication systems and reduce costs.

The Benefits of VoIP for Your Business

As Indiana's largest full-service business technology provider, we at Van Ausdall & Farrar have seen firsthand how VoIP can transform business operations. Here are some of the key benefits:

  1. Cost Savings: VoIP can significantly reduce your phone bills, especially for long-distance and international calls. Since calls are routed over the internet, you're not paying for traditional phone line usage.
  2. Flexibility and Mobility: With VoIP, your office phone can go wherever you go. Whether you're working from home, a coffee shop, or halfway across the world, you can make and receive calls as if you're in the office.
  3. Scalability: As your business grows, VoIP grows with you. Adding new lines or features is typically as simple as a software update, without the need for extensive hardware installations.
  4. Advanced Features: VoIP systems often come with a host of features that traditional phone systems can't match, such as video conferencing, instant messaging, and integration with other business applications.
  5. Improved Customer Service: Features like call routing, voicemail-to-email transcription, and interactive voice response (IVR) can help your team provide better, more efficient customer service.

VoIP and Unified Communications: A Perfect Match

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we believe in creating truly connected and integrated business telephone solutions. That's why we see VoIP as a crucial component of a larger unified communications strategy. Our partnerships with industry leaders like Mitel, 8x8, and RingCentral allow us to offer comprehensive solutions that go beyond just voice calls.

Imagine a system where your phone calls, video conferences, instant messages, and emails all work together seamlessly. That's the power of unified communications, and VoIP is at its heart. Whether you need a simple setup for a single location or a complex multi-office solution with advanced call center capabilities, we can create a system that meets your unique needs.

VoIP in Action: Real-World Applications

Let's look at some ways businesses are leveraging VoIP technology to improve their operations:

  • Remote Work: With the rise of remote and hybrid work models, VoIP has become indispensable. Employees can use their office phone numbers from anywhere, maintaining professionalism and consistency.
  • Call Centers: VoIP technology enables advanced call center solutions, improving customer experiences through features like intelligent call routing and real-time analytics.
  • International Business: For companies with global operations, VoIP can dramatically reduce the cost of international communication while improving call quality.
  • Collaboration: VoIP systems often integrate with collaboration tools, making it easy to transition from a voice call to a video conference or screen-sharing session.

Implementing VoIP: What to Consider

While the benefits of VoIP are clear, implementing a new phone system requires careful planning. Here are some factors to consider:

  1. Internet Connection: VoIP relies on a stable internet connection. Ensure your bandwidth can handle the increased data usage.
  2. Hardware: While many VoIP systems can work with existing phones, you may need to upgrade to IP phones for the best experience.
  3. Security: Like any internet-based technology, VoIP needs proper security measures to protect your communications.
  4. Training: Your team may need training to make the most of the new features available with VoIP.

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we're here to guide you through every step of the process, from initial assessment to implementation and ongoing support.

The Future of VoIP

As we look to the future, we see VoIP becoming even more integrated with other business technologies. Artificial intelligence and machine learning are already being incorporated into VoIP systems, enabling features like real-time language translation and advanced voice analytics.

5G technology is also set to enhance VoIP capabilities, particularly for mobile users. With faster, more reliable connections, we can expect even better call quality and more seamless integration between desktop and mobile VoIP applications.

Conclusion: Embracing the VoIP Revolution

From our humble beginnings as a distributor for the Thomas Edison Company in 1914 to our current position as a leader in business technology solutions, Van Ausdall & Farrar has always been committed to helping businesses leverage the latest innovations. VoIP is more than just a new way to make phone calls. It's a gateway to more efficient, flexible, and cost-effective business communication.

As we continue to navigate the digital age, our mission remains the same: to provide value-driven technology solutions while delivering a world-class customer experience. Whether you're considering implementing VoIP for the first time or looking to upgrade your existing system, we're here to help you make the most of this transformative technology.

Ready to take your business communication to the next level with VoIP? Contact Van Ausdall & Farrar today, and let's work together to create a communication solution that empowers your business for the future.

title: How Cloud Solutions Ensure Business Continuity
htmlTitle: How Cloud Solutions Ensure Business Continuity
author: Van Ausdall & Farrar
featuredImageAlt: Man uploading data onto the cloud
teaser: Before we dive into the nitty-gritty of business continuity, let's take a moment to appreciate what cloud solutions actually are. Reach out to our team today.
metaDescription: Before we dive into the nitty-gritty of business continuity, let's take a moment to appreciate what cloud solutions actually are. Reach out to our team today.
bodyHtml:
Enter cloud solutions, the superhero of modern business continuity. At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we've been helping businesses stay ahead of the curve since 1914, and we're excited to share how cloud technology is revolutionizing the way companies approach disaster recovery and business continuity.

The Silver Lining: Understanding Cloud Solutions

Before we dive into the nitty-gritty of business continuity, let's take a moment to appreciate what cloud solutions actually are. Imagine a magical place where all your data, applications, and infrastructure live, accessible from anywhere, at any time, as long as you have an internet connection. That's the cloud in a nutshell!

Cloud solutions offer businesses the flexibility to store and access their critical information and systems without being tied to physical hardware or specific locations. It's like having a digital safety deposit box that you can reach into whenever you need, wherever you are.

When the Storm Hits: The Importance of Business Continuity

Now, picture this: It's a typical Tuesday at the office. The coffee's brewing, keyboards are clacking, and suddenly, boom! A power outage hits, or worse, a natural disaster strikes. In the pre-cloud era, this could spell disaster for a business. Important files trapped on local servers, communication systems down, and productivity grinding to a halt.

1. Data Backup and Recovery

The Future is in the Cloud

bodyHtml:
Enter MFA, Multi-Factor Authentication, the caped crusader of cybersecurity that's here to save the day!

What is MFA, and Why Should You Care?

MFA is like having a bouncer at the entrance of your favorite nightclub, but instead of checking IDs, it's verifying multiple pieces of evidence before granting access to your digital assets. It's an extra layer of security that goes beyond the traditional username and password combo.

Here at Van Ausdall & Farrar, we've been helping businesses stay ahead of the technology curve since 1914. While we didn't have MFA back when we were distributing for Thomas Edison (imagine if we did, though!), we know it's an essential tool in today's cybersecurity arsenal.

The Three Pillars of MFA

MFA typically relies on three types of authentication factors:

  1. Something you know: This could be a password, PIN, or the answer to a security question. It's information stored in your brain.
  2. Something you have: This might be a smartphone, a security token, or a smart card. It's a physical object in your possession.
  3. Something you are: This refers to biometric data like fingerprints, facial recognition, or retinal scans. It's unique to you and your body.

By combining two or more of these factors, MFA creates a formidable defense against unauthorized access. It's like having a moat, a drawbridge, and a fire-breathing dragon all protecting your digital castle!

Why Your Business Needs MFA

In our century-plus of serving businesses in Indiana and beyond, we've seen technology evolve at breakneck speed. But one thing remains constant: the need for robust security. Here's why MFA should be a no-brainer for your business:

  • Enhanced Security: MFA can prevent 99.9% of automated attacks. That's like having a shield that stops 999 out of 1000 arrows!
  • Regulatory Compliance: Many industries require MFA to meet compliance standards. It's not just smart; it's often mandatory.
  • Customer Trust: Implementing MFA shows your clients that you take their data security seriously. It's a trust-building exercise with tangible benefits.
  • Flexibility: MFA can be customized to fit your specific business needs and user preferences.

MFA and Van Ausdall & Farrar's Solutions

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we're not just about selling technology; we're about implementing solutions that improve the human experience. That's why our Information Technology Solutions include robust MFA options as part of our Managed IT and Cloud Solutions.

Our approach to MFA is holistic, considering how it integrates with your entire IT infrastructure. Here's how we can help:

  • Managed IT Solutions: We can implement and manage MFA across your entire network, ensuring that every access point is secure.
  • Cloud Solutions: Our cloud services come with built-in MFA options, providing an extra layer of security for your cloud-based assets.
  • IT Support: Our team is always ready to assist with MFA setup, troubleshooting, and user training.

MFA Best Practices

Implementing MFA is a great start, but to get the most out of it, consider these best practices:

  1. Use App-Based Authenticators: These are more secure than SMS-based codes.
  2. Implement Across All Systems: Don't leave any access points vulnerable.
  3. Educate Your Team: Make sure everyone understands the importance of MFA and how to use it properly.
  4. Regularly Review and Update: Cyber threats evolve, and so should your MFA strategy.

The Future of MFA

As we look to the future, MFA is evolving to become even more secure and user-friendly. Some exciting developments include:

  • Adaptive MFA: This uses context (like location or device) to determine when additional authentication is needed.
  • Passwordless Authentication: Eliminating passwords altogether in favor of other factors.
  • Biometric Innovations: Advanced biometrics like behavioral analysis and voice recognition.

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we're always keeping an eye on these developments to ensure our clients have access to the latest and greatest in security technology.

Conclusion: Embrace the MFA Superhero

In a world where cyber threats are constantly evolving, MFA stands as a beacon of hope, a digital superhero ready to protect your business from the villains of the cyber world. It's not just a security measure; it's peace of mind.

As we've been doing since 1914, Van Ausdall & Farrar is here to help you navigate the complex world of business technology. Whether you're looking to implement MFA, upgrade your IT infrastructure, or explore new communication solutions, we're your trusted partner in this journey.

Remember, in the digital age, not all heroes wear capes. Some come in the form of a simple yet powerful security protocol. Embrace MFA, and let it be the superhero your business deserves!

The Evolving Threat Landscape

Cyber threats are like a game of whack-a-mole - as soon as you think you've got one under control, another pops up. Hackers and cybercriminals are constantly evolving their tactics, developing new malware, and finding creative ways to exploit vulnerabilities. It's a never-ending battle, but one that businesses must be prepared to fight.

Some of the most common threats include:

  • Ransomware attacks
  • Phishing scams
  • Malware infections
  • Insider threats
  • Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks

Staying ahead of these threats requires a proactive approach to data security. It's not just about building a wall; it's about constantly reinforcing and adapting your defenses.

The Building Blocks of Strong Data Security

Creating a robust data security strategy is like constructing a fortress. You need strong foundations, multiple layers of defense, and vigilant guards. Here are some key components:

1. Employee Education and Training

Your employees are both your first line of defense and potentially your weakest link. Regular training on cybersecurity best practices, such as identifying phishing emails and using strong passwords, is crucial. Think of it as teaching your crew how to spot icebergs before they sink the ship.

2. Strong Access Controls

Implement strict access controls to ensure that employees only have access to the data they need to do their jobs. This includes using strong authentication methods, like multi-factor authentication. It's like having a bouncer at the door of your data vault, checking IDs and only letting in authorized personnel.

3. Regular Software Updates and Patch Management

Keeping your software and systems up-to-date is crucial for closing potential security loopholes. It's like patching holes in your ship's hull before setting sail - you want to make sure you're watertight before you venture into dangerous waters.

4. Robust Backup and Recovery Systems

In the event of a data breach or loss, having reliable backups can be a lifesaver. It's like having a lifeboat on your ship - you hope you never need it, but you'll be glad it's there if disaster strikes.

5. Encryption

Encrypting sensitive data both in transit and at rest adds an extra layer of protection. Even if cybercriminals manage to get their hands on your data, they won't be able to read it without the encryption key. It's like sending messages in a secret code that only trusted parties can decipher.

The Van Ausdall & Farrar Approach to Data Security

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we understand that navigating the complex world of data security can be overwhelming. That's why we offer comprehensive Information Technology Solutions designed to keep your data safe and your business running smoothly.

Our approach includes:

We provide round-the-clock monitoring and management of your IT infrastructure, identifying and addressing potential security threats before they can cause damage. Think of us as your 24/7 security detail, always on the lookout for suspicious activity.

Cloud Solutions

Our secure cloud solutions offer scalable and flexible options for data storage and processing, with built-in security features to protect your information. It's like storing your valuables in a high-tech vault that grows with your needs.

IT Support

Our team of experts is always ready to assist with any security concerns or incidents, providing rapid response and resolution. We're like your personal IT SWAT team, ready to swoop in and save the day at a moment's notice.

The Role of Communication in Data Security

Effective communication is crucial in maintaining strong data security. This includes clear policies and procedures for handling sensitive information, as well as open channels for reporting potential security incidents. Our Communication Solutions can help ensure that your team stays connected and informed about security protocols and potential threats.

Document Security: The Often Overlooked Aspect

While digital data security often takes center stage, it's important not to overlook the security of physical documents. Our Copy / Print Technology solutions include secure printing options to prevent sensitive documents from falling into the wrong hands. Additionally, our Process Management services can help you digitize and securely store physical documents, reducing the risk of data loss or theft.

The Future of Data Security

As technology continues to evolve, so too will the challenges and solutions in data security. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning are increasingly being used to detect and respond to threats in real-time. The Internet of Things (IoT) is expanding the attack surface, requiring new approaches to security. And as more businesses move to the cloud, cloud security will become even more critical.

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we're committed to staying at the forefront of these developments, continually updating our solutions to provide the best possible protection for our clients.

Conclusion: Your Partner in Data Security

UCaaS, or Unified Communications as a Service, is a cloud-based platform that integrates various communication tools into a single, cohesive system. title: Physical Security: How Access Control Protects Your Business

author: Van Ausdall & Farrar

bodyHtml:
It's easy to focus solely on cybersecurity and forget about the importance of physical security. But the truth is, protecting your business from unauthorized access in the real world is just as crucial as safeguarding your digital assets. That's where access control systems come in. They're the unsung heroes of physical security, working tirelessly to keep your premises safe and secure.

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we've been helping businesses stay ahead of the curve since 1914. While we may have started by distributing Thomas Edison's groundbreaking inventions, we've evolved to become Indiana's largest full-service business technology provider. And just as we've adapted to changing times, we understand that your physical security needs are constantly evolving too.

What is Access Control?

Access control is like having a virtual bouncer for your business. It's a system that manages who can enter specific areas of your premises, when they can enter, and under what conditions. Think of it as a high-tech upgrade from the traditional lock-and-key approach.

Modern access control systems can include:

  • Key cards or fobs
  • Biometric scanners (fingerprint, retinal, or facial recognition)
  • PIN pads
  • Mobile phone-based access
  • Integration with video surveillance systems

Why Your Business Needs Access Control

You might be thinking, "We're not Fort Knox, do we really need all this?" The answer is a resounding yes! Here's why:

  1. Enhanced Security: Access control systems provide a robust first line of defense against unauthorized entry, theft, and vandalism.
  2. Employee Tracking: Know who's coming and going, and when. This can be invaluable for time tracking and in the event of an incident.
  3. Visitor Management: Easily manage and monitor guests, contractors, and temporary workers.
  4. Compliance: Many industries have specific security requirements. Access control helps ensure you're meeting these standards.
  5. Flexibility: Easily grant or revoke access privileges as needed, without the hassle of changing locks or collecting keys.

Access Control and Your IT Infrastructure

Now, you might be wondering how access control fits into the broader technology landscape of your business. This is where things get really exciting! Modern access control systems can integrate seamlessly with your existing IT infrastructure, creating a holistic security ecosystem.

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we specialize in Information Technology Solutions, including Managed IT Solutions and Cloud Solutions. This expertise allows us to help you create a unified security strategy that bridges the physical and digital realms.

For example:

  • Integration with HR systems for automatic access provisioning and de-provisioning
  • Cloud-based access control management for multi-site businesses
  • Mobile access capabilities that leverage your employees' smartphones
  • Integration with video surveillance for enhanced monitoring and incident response

Communication is Key

An often-overlooked aspect of access control is how it ties into your overall communication strategy. After all, what good is a secure entrance if you can't communicate with the person trying to gain access?

This is where our expertise in Communication Solutions comes into play. We can help you integrate your access control system with:

  • Intercom systems for visitor screening
  • VoIP phone systems for seamless communication between security personnel and employees
  • Emergency notification systems to alert staff in case of a security breach

Document Security: The Often Forgotten Aspect of Physical Security

When we think about physical security, we often focus on protecting the premises. But what about the sensitive documents within your office? This is where our expertise in Copy / Print Technology and Process Management becomes invaluable.

Consider implementing:

  • Secure printing solutions that require authentication before documents are released
  • Document management systems to track who accesses sensitive files
  • Shredding services to safely dispose of confidential materials

By combining access control with secure document management, you create a comprehensive physical security strategy that protects not just your premises, but the sensitive information within them.

The Human Touch in Access Control

While all this technology is impressive, it's important to remember that the human element is still crucial in any security system. The most sophisticated access control solution won't be effective if your employees don't understand how to use it properly or why it's important.

This is where Van Ausdall & Farrar's commitment to improving the human experience through technology really shines. We don't just install systems, we help you create a culture of security awareness. This might include:

  • Training sessions for employees on proper use of access control systems
  • Development of clear security policies and procedures
  • Regular security audits and drills
  • Ongoing support and troubleshooting

The Future of Access Control

As we look to the future, the world of access control is evolving rapidly. Some exciting trends to watch include:

  • AI and Machine Learning: These technologies can help identify unusual access patterns and potential security threats.
  • IoT Integration: Access control systems are becoming part of the broader Internet of Things, allowing for more comprehensive building management.
  • Touchless Access: In a post-pandemic world, solutions that minimize physical contact are becoming increasingly popular.
  • Behavioral Biometrics: Beyond just recognizing physical characteristics, future systems might analyze behavior patterns for even more secure authentication.

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we're committed to staying at the forefront of these technological advancements. Our goal is to help you implement solutions that not only meet your current needs but are also adaptable to future developments.

Conclusion: Your Partner in Physical Security

Physical security, with access control at its core, is a critical component of your overall business protection strategy. It's not just about keeping the bad guys out. It's about creating a safe, efficient, and compliant environment for your employees and visitors.

As Indiana's largest full-service business technology provider, Van Ausdall & Farrar is uniquely positioned to help you navigate the complex world of access control and physical security. Our expertise spans Information Technology Solutions, Communication Solutions, Copy / Print Technology, and Process Management, all the pieces needed to create a comprehensive, integrated security solution.

Remember, security isn't a one-time installation. It's an ongoing process. As your business grows and evolves, so too should your security measures. With Van Ausdall & Farrar by your side, you can rest assured that your physical security is in good hands, allowing you to focus on what you do best, running your business.

From managing healthcare records to safeguarding financial information, data security is paramount for businesses across industries. At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we're committed to providing best-in-class technology solutions that prioritize robust data protection. That's why we're thrilled to announce that NT-ware, a Canon Group company, has successfully completed the rigorous SOC 2 Type 2 audit for its uniFLOW Online solution.

What is SOC 2 Type 2 Certification?

SOC 2 (Service Organization Control) is a globally recognized auditing standard developed by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA). It evaluates a service organization's information security practices, policies, procedures, and operations to ensure they meet stringent data protection and privacy requirements.

The SOC 2 Type 2 audit goes a step further, assessing the operational effectiveness of these controls over an extended period, typically 12 months. By achieving this certification, NT-ware demonstrates its long-term commitment to safeguarding customer data through comprehensive security measures.

Strengthening Data Protection for uniFLOW Online

UniFLOW Online is a powerful cloud-based solution that streamlines print and scan management across an organization. With this SOC 2 Type 2 certification, customers can be confident that their sensitive data is secured through NT-ware's robust information security controls.

This achievement underscores NT-ware's dedication to implementing industry-leading data protection standards and highlights uniFLOW Online as a trusted solution for managing customer data securely.

This places Van Ausdall & Farrar, Inc. among an elite group of technology providers who have voluntarily chosen to hold themselves to the highest possible cybersecurity standards and protocols, at a time when it matters most.

ISO 27001 is the international gold standard for how organizations should manage information security. While most Managed IT Services Providers (MSPs) operate without clear accountability or regulatory oversight, Van Ausdall & Farrar, Inc. has not only equipped itself with leading technologies, but the company has taken another step for their customers, by committing to third-party validation to prove its practices meet stringent data protection and risk mitigation benchmarks. Van Ausdall & Farrar, Inc. is leveraging the ISO Compliance Program provided by Technology Assurance Group (TAG), an organization of top managed technology services providers with over a $1 billion in annual products and services. TAG's comprehensive processes and protocols will enhance Van Ausdall & Farrar, Inc. 's operations to successfully become ISO 27001 Compliant.

"Unfortunately, we're in an industry where anyone can become a Managed IT Services Provider," said Guillermo Fernandez, VCIO at Van Ausdall & Farrar, Inc. . "You could've been a truck driver yesterday and start calling yourself a technology provider today. What clients don't always realize is that without standards, their cybersecurity is only as strong as the judgment of their technician, whose qualifications are tough to ascertain, especially when most business owners tend to be less technical. Earning ISO 27001 compliance proves we don't just talk about cybersecurity, we execute at the highest level."

For small to mid-sized business owners, the technology industry can feel like the Wild West. ISO 27001 Compliance brings structure, discipline, and most importantly, proof that a provider is proactively managing risk. It typically takes over six months and tens of thousands of dollars to earn this compliance, meaning only a very small minority actually pursue it, with even fewer achieving it.

"ISO 27001 Compliance is especially relevant for our clients in regulated industries like finance, healthcare, or manufacturing, where compliance requirements are becoming even stricter. In fact, in some cases, cybersecurity insurance claims are denied if businesses don't work with qualified Managed IT Services Providers." Fernandez continued, "What sets Van Ausdall & Farrar, Inc. apart isn't just the badge on the wall. It's the expertise, processes, protocols, and globally recognized requirement behind it." While ISO 27001 compliance is one key marker to help business owners to decipher between qualified and unqualified cybersecurity organizations, there are other telltale signs to watch for. For example, if your cybersecurity provider's technology stack is essentially a "one-time, 'set-it-andforget-it'" antivirus program, this might serve as a red flag. Additionally, you should be utilizing multi-factor authentication (MFA), not to mention, rigorous patch management and 24/7 monitoring.

"ISO compliance means we're not guessing. We're not relying on duct tape fixes or shortcuts. We follow a documented, repeatable process that's been validated by third-party auditors," added Fernandez.

While many SMBs still believe they're too small to be a target for cybercrime, the statistics say otherwise. Especially through the proliferation of AI, small businesses need to leverage AIbased technology to outpace cybercriminals. Increasingly, cyber insurance providers and regulatory bodies are beginning to require adherence to standards like ISO 27001, as it provides structure in a wide-open industry. Businesses that can't prove compliance may face denied claims, legal issues, or lost revenue from downtime and breaches.

Working with an ISO 27001- compliant provider like Van Ausdall & Farrar, Inc. ensures that your IT team is not only managing your infrastructure, but also protecting your organization's reputation and continuity, so that you can focus on revenue growth, company culture and the areas of your business which yield returns.

This multi-channel approach allows businesses to meet customers where they are, providing support through their preferred communication method. It's all about creating a seamless, unified communications experience, something we at Van Ausdall & Farrar specialize in.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation are revolutionizing contact centers. From chatbots handling initial inquiries to AI-powered analytics providing real-time insights, these technologies are enhancing efficiency and customer satisfaction.

Protecting sensitive information has become more challenging, and more critical, than ever before. At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we've been helping Indiana businesses navigate technological challenges since 1914, and we've seen firsthand how security awareness training has become an indispensable component of modern business protection strategies.

The Human Element in Cybersecurity

Did you know that, according to recent studies, over 80% of data breaches involve a human element? A single clicked phishing email, a password shared over text, or sensitive information accidentally sent to the wrong recipient can undermine even the most robust security systems.

This is where security awareness training becomes invaluable. Rather than seeing employees as potential security liabilities, proper training transforms your team into your organization's first line of defense against cyber threats.

What Effective Security Awareness Training Covers

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, our comprehensive security awareness training programs address critical areas including:

  • Recognizing Phishing Attempts: Teaching employees to identify suspicious emails before damage occurs

  • Safe Internet Browsing: Identifying potentially harmful websites and downloads
  • Data Handling: Proper procedures for managing sensitive information
  • Mobile Device Security: Protecting company information on smartphones and tablets
  • Social Engineering Awareness: Understanding how manipulative tactics can bypass technical controls

Why Traditional Training Often Falls Short

Many organizations implement security training as a "one-and-done" checkbox item for compliance purposes. However, this approach rarely creates lasting behavior change. Effective security awareness isn't about completing a single training session. It's about fostering a security-conscious culture that becomes second nature.

Since 1914, we've learned that technology solutions work best when they improve the human experience, not complicate it. That's why our security awareness programs are designed to be engaging, relevant, and delivered in digestible formats that respect your team's time while maximizing retention.

title: VoIP: Revolutionizing Business Communications in the Digital Age

author: Van Ausdall & Farrar

bodyHtml:
Effective communication is more crucial than ever. Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) has emerged as a game-changing technology that's transforming how businesses connect, collaborate, and communicate. As we at Van Ausdall & Farrar have witnessed since our founding in 1914, communication technology continually evolves, and VoIP represents one of the most significant advancements in recent decades.

What is VoIP and Why Does it Matter?

At its core, VoIP is a technology that allows voice calls to be made using an internet connection rather than a traditional phone line. But it's so much more than just making calls over the internet. VoIP transforms your business phone system into a versatile communications hub that integrates with your other business applications and processes.

For Indiana businesses ranging from small operations to large enterprises, VoIP offers tremendous advantages in flexibility, scalability, and cost-effectiveness compared to legacy phone systems. As businesses continue to embrace remote and hybrid work models, VoIP's ability to connect team members regardless of location has become increasingly valuable.

Key Benefits of VoIP for Your Business

Cost Savings

One of the most immediate benefits businesses notice when switching to VoIP is significant cost reduction. Traditional phone systems often require expensive hardware installations and maintenance, plus separate charges for long-distance calls. VoIP typically reduces these costs by 30-50% by leveraging your existing internet connection and offering all-inclusive calling plans.

Enhanced Mobility

VoIP untethers your team from their desks. With VoIP, employees can make and receive calls from anywhere with an internet connection using their business number. Whether working from home, visiting clients, or traveling between your Indianapolis headquarters and satellite offices, your team maintains seamless communication with clients and colleagues.

Advanced Features

Modern VoIP systems include features that would be expensive add-ons with traditional systems:

  • Auto-attendants and call routing
  • Voicemail-to-email transcription
  • Call analytics and reporting
  • Video conferencing integration
  • CRM integration
  • Instant messaging and presence indicators

Scalability

As your business grows, VoIP grows with you without major infrastructure investments. Adding new users or locations is as simple as provisioning new phones or softphones, perfect for businesses experiencing growth or seasonal fluctuations.

VoIP Implementation: More Than Just Plugging In Phones

While VoIP offers tremendous benefits, successful implementation requires careful planning and expertise. At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we've guided countless Indiana businesses through this transition since VoIP technology first emerged. A successful implementation considers:

  • Network Infrastructure: Ensuring your network can handle the added voice traffic without compromising quality
  • Security: Implementing proper measures to protect your voice communications from cybersecurity threats
  • Business Continuity: Creating redundancies to maintain communications even during outages
  • User Training: Helping your team maximize the new features and capabilities

The Van Ausdall & Farrar Approach to VoIP

Since 1914, we've maintained our position as Indiana's largest full-service business technology provider by evolving alongside technology while keeping customer success at the center of everything we do. Our approach to VoIP exemplifies this philosophy.

Through our strategic partnerships with communication leaders like Mitel, 8x8, Fortinet, and Extreme, we create truly connected and integrated business telephone solutions. Whether you need a basic system for a single location or a sophisticated multi-office contact center with advanced application integration, we design solutions that address your specific business challenges.

Our process begins with understanding your communication workflows, pain points, and goals. We then design a solution that leverages best-in-class products and technologies tailored to your needs. After implementation, our vendor-certified service fleet provides ongoing support throughout Indianapolis and across Indiana.

Beyond Basic VoIP: Unified Communications

For many organizations, VoIP is just the beginning of a broader unified communications strategy. By integrating voice with video, messaging, presence, and collaboration tools, businesses create seamless communication experiences that enhance productivity and customer service.

As specialists in both Communication Solutions and Information Technology Solutions, Van Ausdall & Farrar is uniquely positioned to help your business leverage VoIP as part of a comprehensive technology strategy that may include cloud solutions, managed IT services, and process management.

Ready to Transform Your Business Communications?

Whether you're considering your first VoIP implementation or looking to enhance your existing system, Van Ausdall & Farrar has been helping Indiana businesses harness the power of new technologies for over a century. Our mission remains constant: to provide value-driven technology solutions while delivering a world-class customer experience.

The future of business communication is here - and it's more connected, flexible, and powerful than ever before. Let's explore how VoIP can help your organization communicate more effectively in today's digital business landscape.

What is Content Management, Anyway?

Think of it as a super-powered filing cabinet for the 21st century, capable of handling everything from documents and images to videos and social media posts.

But content management isn't just about tidying up your digital space. It's about creating a system that allows you to:

  • Find information quickly and easily
  • Collaborate with team members seamlessly
  • Ensure compliance with regulations
  • Improve security and reduce risk
  • Automate repetitive tasks
  • Make better business decisions based on data

In short, it's about making your business run smoother than a freshly waxed slip-n-slide.

The Van Ausdall & Farrar Approach: Your Content Management Superhero

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we don't just sell content management solutions - we're your partners in taming the information beast. Our team of experts works with you to understand your unique needs, challenges, and opportunities. Then, like a team of digital architects, we design and build a custom content management solution that fits your business like a glove.

Our approach focuses on three key areas that are crucial for any business:

1. Security: Fort Knox for Your Data

Remember when the most secure place for your documents was a locked filing cabinet? Those days are long gone. In today's digital world, security threats lurk around every corner of the internet. That's why our content management solutions are designed with security in mind.

We implement robust access controls, encryption, and audit trails to ensure that your sensitive information stays safe from prying eyes. It's like having a digital bouncer for your data - only the VIPs (Very Important Personnel) get past the velvet rope.

Our solutions include features like automated retention schedules, audit trails, and e-discovery tools to make compliance a breeze. It's like having a legal team in your pocket, minus the expensive suits.

Whether you're looking to speed up your accounts payable, reduce time-to-hire in HR, or eliminate those pesky late fees, our automation solutions can help. It's like having a tireless, super-efficient robot assistant (without the risk of a robot uprising, of course).

Real-World Benefits: Content Management in Action

Businesses face an ever-growing array of cybersecurity threats. From sneaky malware to sophisticated hacking attempts, the need for robust security measures has never been more critical. One essential component of a comprehensive cybersecurity strategy is intrusion detection. At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we understand the importance of keeping your business safe from digital intruders, and we're here to shed some light on this crucial topic.

What is Intrusion Detection?

Intrusion detection is like having a vigilant digital security guard for your network. It's a system designed to monitor network traffic and system activities for any suspicious behavior or policy violations. Think of it as a high-tech alarm system for your business's digital assets.

There are two main types of intrusion detection systems (IDS):

  1. Network-based IDS (NIDS): These systems monitor traffic on entire networks or specific segments.
  2. Host-based IDS (HIDS): These focus on individual devices or endpoints within a network.

Both types work tirelessly to identify potential security breaches, unauthorized access attempts, and other malicious activities that could compromise your business's data and operations.

Why is Intrusion Detection Important?

Data is the lifeblood of most businesses. Whether it's customer information, financial records, or proprietary research, protecting this valuable asset is paramount. Intrusion detection systems play a crucial role in this protection by:

  • Identifying potential security threats in real-time

title: Beyond Passwords: Why Multi-Factor Authentication Is Your Business's Security Superpower
htmlTitle: Beyond Passwords: Why Multi-Factor Authentication Wins
author: Van Ausdall & Farrar
featuredImageAlt: Man using tablet with data protection digital icons on it
teaser: Where cyber threats lurk around every corner, relying solely on passwords is like securing your office with a screen door. Talk to our specialists for guidance.
metaDescription: Where cyber threats lurk around every corner, relying solely on passwords is like securing your office with a screen door. Talk to our specialists for guidance.
bodyHtml:
Where cyber threats lurk around every corner, relying solely on passwords is like securing your office with a screen door. As technology evolves, so do the methods hackers use to breach your systems. That's where Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) comes in - a security approach that's become less of a luxury and more of a necessity for businesses of all sizes.

What Is Multi-Factor Authentication?

Multi-factor authentication is a security method that requires users to provide two or more verification factors to gain access to a resource such as an application, online account, or VPN. Rather than just asking for a password (something you know), MFA requires additional proof of identity, which might include:

  • Something you have - like a smartphone for receiving verification codes
  • Something you are - biometric verification such as a fingerprint or facial recognition
  • Something you know - a PIN or the answer to a security question
  • Somewhere you are - geolocation verification

This layered approach to security makes it significantly more difficult for unauthorized users to access your sensitive information, even if they manage to steal or guess your password.

Why Your Business Needs MFA Now

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we've seen firsthand how implementing MFA has protected our clients from potential breaches. Here's why it's crucial:

Passwords Alone Are Vulnerable

Even "strong" passwords can be compromised. Research shows that 81% of data breaches are due to weak or stolen passwords. With MFA, a stolen password alone isn't enough to gain access.

Remote Work Has Expanded the Attack Surface

With more employees working remotely on various networks, the potential entry points for cyberattacks have multiplied. MFA provides consistent security regardless of where your team works.

Compliance Requirements

Many regulatory frameworks now require MFA implementation. For industries dealing with sensitive information, it's often no longer optional.

Protection Against Sophisticated Attacks

Phishing schemes and social engineering tactics grow more convincing by the day. MFA adds a layer of protection against these deceptive approaches.

Implementing MFA: Easier Than You Think

Many business leaders worry that adding MFA will create friction in their workflows or frustrate employees. However, when implemented properly, MFA can be both secure and user-friendly.

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, our IT Solutions team specializes in deploying MFA systems that balance robust security with ease of use. We understand that technology should enhance the human experience, not complicate it - a principle that's been guiding us since 1914.

MFA Options for Modern Businesses

Today's MFA solutions offer flexibility to suit different business needs:

  • SMS or Email Verification - Codes sent to trusted devices
  • Authenticator Apps - Generate time-based codes without needing cell service
  • Biometric Authentication - Fingerprint or facial recognition
  • Hardware Tokens - Physical devices that generate authentication codes
  • Push Notifications - One-tap approval on registered mobile devices

How Van Ausdall & Farrar Can Help

As Indiana's largest full-service business technology provider, we don't just sell solutions - we implement technology that improves security while enhancing workflow efficiency. Our Managed IT Solutions team can:

  • Assess your current security posture and vulnerability points
  • Design an MFA strategy tailored to your business needs and industry requirements
  • Implement cloud-based or on-premises MFA solutions that integrate with your existing systems
  • Train your team on best practices for using MFA effectively
  • Provide ongoing support and management through our comprehensive IT Support services

We've helped organizations across healthcare, insurance, government, manufacturing, and more implement effective MFA strategies that protect sensitive information without disrupting productivity.

Beyond MFA: A Comprehensive Security Approach

While MFA is a critical component of modern cybersecurity, it works best as part of a layered security strategy. Our team can help you integrate MFA within a comprehensive approach that includes:

  • Secure network solutions
  • Cloud security measures
  • Content management systems with appropriate access controls
  • Document and device security through our Managed Print Services

Since 1914, Van Ausdall & Farrar has evolved alongside technology to keep Indiana businesses secure and efficient. From our beginnings with Thomas Edison's company to today's sophisticated digital landscape, our mission remains consistent: providing value-driven technology solutions while delivering a world-class customer experience.

Ready to strengthen your organization's security with multi-factor authentication? Contact Van Ausdall & Farrar today to discuss how our IT Solutions team can help protect your business while improving workflow efficiency - because security doesn't have to come at the expense of productivity.

title: Weather The Storm: How Cloud Solutions Ensure Business Continuity No Matter What
htmlTitle: Cloud Solutions for Business Continuity in Any Storm
author: Van Ausdall & Farrar
teaser: But what if your business could continue functioning smoothly regardless of what challenges come your way? Talk to our team about the right solution for you.
metaDescription: But what if your business could continue functioning smoothly regardless of what challenges come your way? Talk to our team about the right solution for you.
bodyHtml:
Continuity isn't just a nice-to-have - it's essential for survival. From natural disasters to technical failures and even unexpected global events (remember 2020?), organizations face countless threats that can disrupt operations. But what if your business could continue functioning smoothly regardless of what challenges come your way?

That's where cloud solutions enter the picture, offering a resilience that traditional on-premise systems simply cannot match. At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we've been helping Indiana businesses navigate technological changes since 1914, and we've seen firsthand how cloud adoption has transformed business continuity planning.

The "Always On" Advantage

Remember the days when a server crash meant your entire operation ground to a halt? Cloud solutions have fundamentally changed this equation by removing single points of failure. When your critical applications and data reside in the cloud, they're typically hosted across multiple redundant servers in geographically diverse locations.

This means that even if one data center experiences issues, your services automatically transition to functioning servers elsewhere - often so seamlessly that your team never even notices the hiccup. No downtime. No data loss. No panicked calls to IT in the middle of the night.

Work From Anywhere, Anytime

If the past few years have taught us anything, it's that flexibility in where and how we work isn't just convenient - it's sometimes necessary. Cloud-based systems enable your employees to access critical business applications and information from virtually anywhere with an internet connection.

This isn't just about working from home during a pandemic. It means your sales team can access customer information while on the road. Your executives can approve critical documents while at conferences. Your support staff can resolve customer issues whether they're in the office or working remotely. The cloud essentially creates a virtual workplace that exists wherever your people need it to be.

Scalability That Grows With Your Needs

Traditional on-premise systems required significant capital investment and planning to scale up. Need more storage? Order new hardware, wait for delivery, schedule installation time, and hope you've estimated your needs correctly.

Cloud solutions flip this model entirely. Need more resources? They're available instantly. Experiencing seasonal demand? Scale up during busy periods and scale down when things quiet down. This flexibility ensures your business can respond quickly to changing market conditions without overprovisioning resources "just in case."

Disaster Recovery Made Simple

Before cloud solutions, comprehensive disaster recovery plans were incredibly complex and costly - often out of reach for small and mid-sized businesses. The cloud has democratized disaster recovery, making robust backup and restoration capabilities accessible to organizations of all sizes.

With cloud-based backup solutions, your data is automatically backed up at regular intervals without manual intervention. If disaster strikes, recovery is faster and more complete. Rather than spending days restoring from tape backups (if they're even accessible), cloud recovery can often be completed in hours or even minutes.

Enhanced Security Posture

Many businesses are surprised to learn that cloud solutions often provide better security than on-premise alternatives. Major cloud providers invest millions in physical and cybersecurity measures that would be cost-prohibitive for individual organizations to implement.

From advanced encryption and multi-factor authentication to round-the-clock security monitoring and immediate security patching, cloud providers offer enterprise-grade security to businesses of all sizes. When implemented correctly, cloud solutions can significantly enhance your overall security posture - an essential component of business continuity.

How Van Ausdall & Farrar Can Help

At Van Ausdall & Farrar, we've spent over a century helping Indiana businesses leverage technology to overcome challenges and achieve their goals. Our Cloud Solutions team specializes in designing and implementing cloud strategies that ensure your business continues to operate smoothly no matter what obstacles arise.

Whether you're looking to migrate existing systems to the cloud, implement hybrid cloud solutions, or enhance your existing cloud infrastructure with better security and redundancy, our experts can help. We take the time to understand your specific business needs and design solutions that provide continuity without unnecessary complexity or cost.

Our approach aligns perfectly with our mission: to provide value-driven technology solutions while delivering a world-class customer experience. By implementing cloud technologies that improve business continuity, we're helping to fulfill our vision of using technology to improve the human experience, because nothing disrupts the human experience quite like system downtime and data loss.

Taking The Next Step

Business continuity isn't something you need until suddenly, critically, you do. Rather than waiting for disaster to strike, proactive organizations are leveraging cloud solutions now to ensure they're prepared for whatever challenges tomorrow may bring.

If you're ready to weather any storm with confidence, reach out to our team at Van Ausdall & Farrar. With our comprehensive Cloud Solutions, Communication Solutions, IT Support, and Process Management services, we can help ensure your business never misses a beat, regardless of what challenges come your way.

Because in today's business environment, the question isn't if disruption will occur, but when. And with the right cloud strategy in place, your answer to disruption can simply be: "Business as usual."

title: Successfully Implementing Data Retention Policies for Local Businesses
htmlTitle: How Local Businesses Implement Data Retention Policies
author: Van Ausdall & Farrar
featuredImageAlt: Man working on laptop with a cup of coffe next to him
teaser: Leading MTSP Helps Organizations Avoid Penalties Due to Poor Data Management Practices INDIANAPOLIS, IN... Contact us today to learn more about your options.
metaDescription: Leading MTSP Helps Organizations Avoid Penalties Due to Poor Data Management Practices INDIANAPOLIS, IN... Contact us today to learn more about your options.
bodyHtml:
Leading MTSP Helps Organizations Avoid Penalties Due to Poor Data Management Practices

INDIANAPOLIS, IN ‐Van Ausdall & Farrar, Inc, a leading managed technology services provider (MTSP), is helping small to mid-sized businesses (SMBs) avoid costly penalties and fines associated with poor data management policies. As more organizations have been publicly affected by cyberattacks in the mainstream news, governments have responded by increasing their scrutiny on the IT and data management practices of SMBs across the nation. Since the public has growing concerns over data privacy, governments are enforcing stricter laws to ensure compliance across a wide array of industries and having an effective, comprehensive data retention policy is vital to ensure compliance. As a result, Van Ausdall & Farrar, Inc. is proactively educating and protecting local businesses from being struck with financial, civil or even criminal penalties, especially when all those costs are so unnecessary.

Data retention policies are under much more scrutiny than ever before because the public has grown weary of lackluster cybersecurity measures, frequent data breaches and the common misuse of personal data. In other words, governments are starting to increase the pressure they place on SMBs to adhere to strict regulations to keep end users' data protected. One of the clearest ways to demonstrate that your organization has addressed these concerns is by organizing your data and giving it structure through a data retention policy. Guillermo Fernandez, VCIO at Van Ausdall & Farrar stated, "The core concept to understand is data now has a 'shelf life.' If data is stored improperly, irresponsibly or negligently, regulators are not taking it lightly anymore. For example, depending on which industry you're in, you need to understand how long you're legally permitted to store certain data. In some industries you're permitted to store customer credit card details, but in others you cannot store certain details, like the CVV/CVC 'code on the back' to remain in compliance. With stricter regulations coming down from the federal government, we're trying to advise as many business owners as possible to keep them educated, compliant and penalty-free."

Another example of a precarious regulation that business owners commonly overlook is the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), which can cost businesses up to $7,500 if they deliberately violate a California consumer's data privacy rights, regardless of where the company's is located. In other words, even if your business is not based in California but you merely have a couple customers from there, you could be penalized for not adhering to these data policies. While compliance is the main driver compelling businesses to reevaluate their data retention policies, there are plenty of other reasons to keep sensitive data well-organized. Here are a few areas SMBs should consider when setting up their data retention policies:

  1. Cost Reduction - Most employees will default to storing every piece of data they ever create. Without thinking, this can lead to bloated networks, underperforming technology and ultimately, significant storage costs. Data retention policies should include a segmentation and prioritization process of datasets to ensure that the right data is saved and easily accessible, and obsolete data is discarded so the company is continually reducing its liability in the event of a breach.
  2. Quicker Recovery from Outages - In the event of an outage, employees need to be able to recover data quickly so the business can resume operations without causing unnecessary downtime. Taking the time to set up a data retention policy enables employees to more easily access key data, streamlining recovery/flexibility. Essentially, outages only cause downtime if the organization is already underprepared in the first place. A robust data retention policy can limit these risks and limit a company's recovery time back to full capacity.
  3. Hybrid Storage - Many businesses face challenges when they attempt to digitize all of their records (especially when it comes to cloud integrations) and wind up having partial records in digital form, whereas other records are still on paper. Obviously, this can lead to unbalanced data policies, which may appear to limit liability, however, in effect they only make a bigger mess. This is another reason why it's so important to have a data retention policy established, so that you can ensure effective records management regardless of which mediums you use to maintain your records.

The mountains of paper documents that once defined office environments are quickly becoming relics of the past. Yet many businesses still struggle with rooms full of filing cabinets and boxes of records that consume valuable space and resources. Document conversion services offer a powerful solution to this common challenge, bringing efficiency, accessibility, and security to your information management processes. Let's explore how transitioning from paper to digital can revolutionize your business operations.

Reclaiming Your Valuable Office Space

The cost of commercial real estate continues to climb, making every square foot of your office a significant investment. When you're dedicating entire rooms to store paper documents, you're essentially paying premium rates for inactive storage space. With the shift toward hybrid work models, businesses are reconsidering how their physical office space can better serve their evolving needs.

Converting paper documents to digital formats allows you to transform cluttered file rooms into productive areas that support your business goals. Those walls of filing cabinets could become collaborative workspaces, meeting areas, or comfortable workstations for your hybrid employees. The transformation not only creates a more modern, efficient workplace but also significantly reduces your real estate costs per productive square foot.

Enhanced Searchability and Records Management

How much time do your employees spend searching for specific information in paper files? Minutes? Hours? Days? This hidden cost of paper-based systems drains productivity and creates frustration.

Digital document conversion solves this problem by making your records instantly searchable. Through Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology, the content within your documents becomes indexable and searchable, allowing employees to find exactly what they need with a simple keyword search. What once took hours now takes seconds.

Additionally, digital systems make records management and retention policies easier to implement and maintain. You can set automatic retention schedules, receive notifications about documents nearing their destruction dates, and maintain compliance with regulatory requirements, all without the manual tracking and physical handling that paper-based systems require.

Supporting Your Distributed Workforce

The rise of remote and hybrid work arrangements has exposed a critical weakness in paper-based document systems: accessibility. When important documents are physically locked in an office file room, remote employees simply cannot access them without someone physically present to retrieve, scan, and send the information.

Document conversion creates a secure digital repository that authorized employees can access from anywhere at any time. This accessibility doesn't just support your remote workforce, it empowers them, enabling collaboration and decision-making regardless of physical location. The result is a more agile organization capable of responding to opportunities and challenges without the delays inherent in paper-based systems.

As a business technology provider partnering with industry leaders like Opex, Fujitsu, Canon, Hyland OnBase, Square9 Softworks, and Ephesoft, we're uniquely positioned to recommend and implement solutions tailored to your specific needs.

Beyond Simple Scanning

Document conversion is more than just creating digital copies of paper documents. When implemented strategically, it becomes a catalyst for business process improvement.
